tagline: Leader in data center AI and high-performance computing
hero_kpi_rationale: Data center revenue is AMD's main growth driver, fueled by strong demand for AI chips and servers with 5th-generation EPYC and Instinct MI350 GPUs, positioning AMD as a direct challenger to Nvidia in the generative AI wave.

ai_positioning.summary: AMD positions itself as an AI leader by building a complete AI product portfolio (Instinct GPUs, EPYC CPUs, networking solutions) and developing a proprietary software ecosystem (ROCm) for AI workloads.

evidence.text: AMD Instinct MI350X Series GPUs deployed by hyperscalers in 2025, with annual leadership roadmap for AMD Instinct solutions
Launch of the 5th generation AMD EPYC family in 2025 offering leadership performance for data center workloads including AI
Data center portfolio expansion with AI networking solutions: AMD Pensando Pollara 400 AI NICs and Vulcano AI NICs for high-speed GPU cluster connectivity
Helios AI rack-scale platform integrating CPUs, GPUs and Networking to address growing AI compute needs
6-gigawatt agreement with OpenAI to deploy AMD Instinct MI450 series GPUs, with first gigawatt deployment underway
Strategic acquisitions (ZT Systems for $3.2B) to advance software capabilities in compiler, machine learning, inference and AI performance optimization

kpis.name: Data Center Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by processors and GPUs for data centers, primarily used in AI and cloud computing.
kpis.description: In 2025, the data center segment generated $16.6 billion in revenue, up 32% from $12.6 billion in 2024, driven by strong demand for 5th generation AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs.

kpis.name: AI and HPC Revenue Component (Data Center Segment)
kpis.explanation: Revenue tied to high-performance computing and AI solutions, included within and not separate from data center segment, key for future growth.
kpis.description: AI and HPC revenue is a component of the data center segment, which reached $16.6 billion in 2025, driven by Instinct MI350 Series GPUs dedicated to generative AI workloads.

kpis.name: Total Net Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue — total sales generated over the period.
kpis.description: Total net revenue reached $34.6 billion in 2025, compared to $25.8 billion in 2024, representing 34% year-over-year growth driven by data center and client/gaming segments.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Gross Margin — gross profit divided by revenue.
kpis.description: Gross margin improved to 50.0% in 2025 from 49.3% in 2024, primarily due to favorable product mix, partially offset by approximately $440 million of net inventory and related charges associated with U.S. government export controls on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products.

kpis.name: R&D Intensity
kpis.explanation: R&D spending as a percentage of net revenue, reflecting investment in AI and new product development.
kpis.description: R&D expenses reached $8.091 billion in 2025, representing 23.4% of net revenue, compared to $6.456 billion or 25.0% in 2024, reflecting disciplined investment in AI and product roadmaps as revenue growth outpaced R&D spending increases.

kpis.name: Capex Intensity
kpis.description: Capital expenditures totaled $974 million in 2025, representing 2.8% of net revenue, compared to $645 million or 2.5% in 2024, supporting capacity expansion and infrastructure investments.

company_description: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. operates as a semiconductor company internationally. It operates in three segments: Data Center, Client and Gaming, and Embedded. The company offers artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators, microprocessors, and graphics processing units (GPUs) as standalone devices or as incorporated into accelerated processing units, chipsets, and data center and professional GPUs; and embedded processors and semi-custom system-on-chip (SoC) products, microprocessor and SoC development services and technology, data processing units, field programmable gate arrays (FPGA), system on modules, AI network interface cards, and adaptive SoC products. It provides processors under the AMD Ryzen, AMD Ryzen AI, AMD Ryzen PRO, AMD Ryzen Threadripper, AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO, AMD Athlon, and AMD PRO A-Series brands; graphics under the AMD Radeon graphics and AMD Embedded Radeon graphics; professional graphics under the AMD Radeon Pro graphics brand; and AI and general-purpose compute infrastructure for hyperscale providers. The company offers data center graphics under the AMD Instinct accelerators and Radeon PRO V-series brands; server microprocessors under the AMD EPYC brand
